text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZIL TO LAUNCH GLOBAL BONUS OF $1 BLN
Brazil is preparing itself to launch any time soon a new "global" bonus worth up to $1 billion depending on demand.
-- PETROBRAS ANTICIPATES OPENING OF MARKET
State-owned oil giant Petrobras is readying itself for the opening of the oil sector and is negotiating the opening of the market for a number of derivatives.
-- IFC TO SUPPORT BRAZIL PRIVATIZATION PROGRAM

The World Bank-affiliated International Finance Corporation which provides funding to the private sector in the form of loans and risk capital wants to support the Brazilian privatization process in the infrastructure sector.
O GLOBO
-- ANAETHSTETIC LEAVES MODEL CLAUDIA LIZ IN COMA
Model Claudia Liz has fallen into a deep coma at a Sao Paulo hospital due to complications with the anaesthetic used during a liposuction operation on her stomach.
-- BRAZIL CREDIT RATING IMPROVING ABROAD
Prices of Brazilian shares have risen abroad on rumors that credit rating agencies like Moody's and Standard & Poor's are to improve their assessment of Brazil.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- SAO PAULO SUFFERS SERIES OF BLITZ KIDNAPPINGS
Sao Paulo is experiencing a wave of so-called blitz kidnappings in which the abductors want to negotiate and free their victims the same day in exchange for a moderate amount of money.
-- FEDERAL SUPREME COURT APPROVES CPMF TAX
Brazil's Federal Supreme Court has voted nine to two that the CPMF tax levied on financial transactions is not unconstitutional.
-- PPB AND PMDB CAUSE DELAY OF RE-ELECTION DEBATE
The advocates of a constitutional amendment to allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for a second term have delayed the debate on the issue to win the support of the PPB and PMDB parties.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
